children: shares rose nearly 2.5% in after-hours trading Tuesday after Chief Executive Ryan Cohen bought about $22.77 million of the retailer's stock.
SEC records show Cohen acquired 844,130 shares at prices ranging from $26.75 to $27 each. The purchase was his second reported buy this month, after he spent about $17.1 million on shares on Oct. 2.
Following the transaction, Cohen directly held about 42.49 million shares. Including warrants, his beneficial ownership totals approximately 46.2 million shares, equal to about 9.1% of GameStop.

His continued buying comes after several purchases in September and October as the company pursues growth beyond traditional video game retail. Analyst Daniel Ives recently began coverage with a Buy rating and $32 price target, implying 17.6% upside from the level cited in the report. Ives pointed to collectibles, trading cards and capital allocation as potential drivers of a broader business model. GameStop's $56 billion proposal to buy eBay was rejected earlier this year, and reports later pointed to possible partnership talks.

title: GameStop Stock Jumps Nearly 3% After CEO Drops $22.8 Million on Shares
